messages.subject: Re: Help! Best practices for deploying app
messages.subject_clean: Help! Best practices for deploying app
messages.body_plain:
My personal feeling is that Github (or a similar platform) has great features to help with this, especially if you hook it into a CI server as well.

If you manage all your code on with version control like Github, the only way to get your code from the "develop" branch (where work takes place) into the "master" branch (which is the live, deployed version) is to successfully complete a merge via a pull request. You can build as much structure around this process as you want. A typical workflow might be:
User wants to work on a new feature.
User creates a specific branch to contain changes to the code that relate to this feature.
User finishes their work and is ready to get feedback and incorporate the new feature.
User creates a pull request from their feature branch into develop
Other users review their work, and give feedback. User can add more changes into the pull request until everyone is happy.
The feature branch is merged into develop and the pull request is closed.
When the group is ready to promote the current develop version to the live environment, a pull request is created that will merge the develop branch into the master branch.
After any feedback and corrections, the group is happy that develop is safe to deploy live, and the merge is completed and the pull request is closed. Live now incorporates User's new feature.
This is a very long-winded description of the formal code management practice; it needn't be a very time-consuming process if the feedback rounds are fast. This process can be used for anything from 2 people working on a presentation to hundreds of people working on Youtube's back-end code. This process avoids the situation where changes get pushed live without anyone noticing. In the event of catastrophe, the version control system allows you to roll back to a previous version very easily.

Another major advantage of using tools for this is that many steps can be automated. You can set up a Continuous Integration server that will validate every single commit and pull request by running scripts or processes you define. For work on an R package this might be running R CMD Check and then Building the package. For a shiny dashboard, it could be successfully passing unit tests defined with the testthat package. If you have a rule that no pull request can be merged if its tests are failing, and your tests are set up well, then you ensure that no code that causes breaking changes slips through the net and gets merged by accident. If that ever does happen, you can improve your tests to stop it happening again.

Finally, you can set up automated deployment. You can have your CI server, or some other service, monitor the master branch constantly for updates. As soon as you merge that PR into master, the service will update the server for you without you having to do anything manually. You can roll back just by reverting the master branch. You can have other environments set up to track other branches - a development environment tracking develop, a specific QA/UAT environment tracking a particular branch, and even environments set to track specific feature branches if you want. With everything being automatically tested and then deployed if the tests pass, you can speed up your development processes a lot.

There is tons of advice, training, books, courses, and much more about these sorts of processes. Developing a shiny project is no different to any other software project in these things, so you can use the tools that are already available to you. I hope this helped :)

messages.subject: Syncing two leaflet maps on different tabs.
messages.subject_clean: Syncing two leaflet maps on different tabs.
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

It is possible to sync two maps on different tabs in RMarkdown via Shiny with leaflet?

I asked the question on StackOverflow and was told "probably need to write it in javaScript". Here is a link to the question: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/38023085/sync-two-leaftlet-maps-on-different-tabs-in-rmarkdown-with-shiny/38027320#38027320

Here is a MWE if you put in RMarkdown (if you zoom in on map1, I was to mirror the zoom on map 2):

---
title: "QuestionforStackOverflow"
output:
flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
runtime: shiny
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
```

Tab One
======================================================================
```{r tab1}
output$map1 <-
   renderLeaflet(
    leaflet() %>%
      addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") %>%
      setView(-93.65, 42.0285, zoom = 4)
  )

leafletOutput("map1")

```
Tab Two
======================================================================
```{r tab2}

output$map2 <-
  renderLeaflet(
    leaflet() %>%
      addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") %>%
      setView(-93.65, 42.0285, zoom = 4)
  )

leafletOutput("map2")
```

Thank you,

John

    leaflet() %>%
      addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") %>%
      setView(-93.65, 42.0285, zoom = 4)
  )

actionButton("syncMap1", "Fit to map2 bounds")
leafletOutput("map1")

  map2coords <- input$map2_bounds

messages.subject: Re: Another shiny server
messages.subject_clean: Another shiny server
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joel,

Thanks for your comments.

Serve the app specific files are more complicated, I decided not to support this feature.

The only way I can think of is send 302 redirection to static files, this will increase the time while save the traffic. Another issue is to detect if the files are really static and monitor if they are changed (packages upgrade)

For SEO, please refer to the recommendation (deprecated) for ajax-driven pages.

https://developers.google.com/webmasters/ajax-crawling/docs/learn-more#an-agreement-between-crawler-and-server

I think websocket pages are similar to ajax-driven pages. You need to take a snapshot when the page is loaded completely, and serve bots with this snapshot. It can not be done with the server, a browser is needed to render the page.

The jShiny-Server is released, you may want to try it.

Regards,

Fan

messages.subject: Re: Deoplying Shiny Apps to self-hosted Shiny Server
messages.subject_clean: Deoplying Shiny Apps to self-hosted Shiny Server
messages.body_plain:
You'll need to build your own pipe to your shiny server. "Deploying the app" is just copying the files into the right directory on the server and setting up the correct permissions, but "the right directory" and "the correct permissions" will depend on your configuration; there's no way RStudio could anticipate every possible configuration so it can't be automatic like with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

My suggestion would be to keep your code in some kind of version-control system like Github, and set the server to track a branch - either by polling for updates every now and again and downloading new files if there's a change on the branch, or by some CI service handling the update messages and pushing the files out to the server. You will still have to configure the permissions yourself.

A simpler but far less robust alternative is just to FTP your files onto the server; if your configuration is set up right it will just start working.

messages.subject_clean: 'tkrplot' package error stops shiny from deploying on shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
Unfortunately you can't deploy shiny applications that rely on any packages that need access to the display (such as Tk).  These applications cannot be hosted on Shiny Server, Shiny Server Pro, and shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>  The idea is that shiny applications render themselves within a browser, while Tk presumes that it has access to the graphics display itself which of course on a server, would run on the server, and not within the client's browser.

Ann, the issue you are seeing is probably related to a package that you are using within your application which relies on the tkrplot package being installed.

Hope this helps.

messages.subject_clean: Cyrillic characters are not displayed on ggplot in web app
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Here is the app:

https://zhitkovk.shinyapps.io/russiaincolour/

User is allowed to enter his own plot title ("Название графика" in app) and legend title ("Легенда" in app). After he enters it new plot is displayed. The problem is that when run locally the cyrillic characters are displayed on the plot, but the web app refuses to do so.

My server.R:

# Libraries
source("libraries.R")

# Data is read only once when the app is started
source("read_data.R")

# Function for plotting map
source("map_plotter.R")

# options(shiny.usecairo = TRUE)

shinyServer(
  function(input, output) {

    output$myplot <- renderPlot({
      mapPlotter(ggrmap, input$data_selector,  enc2native(input$text_title),  enc2native(input$text_legend))
    })
  }
)

ui.R :

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Региональные данные на карте"),

  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("data_selector", label = h3("Выберите данные"),
                choices = c("pop_2015", "value")),
    textInput("text_title", label = h4("Название графика"), value = "Регионы России"),
    textInput("text_legend", label = h4("Легенда"), value = "Доля:")
  ),

  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("myplot")
  )
))

Function used for plotting:

mapPlotter <- function(data, fill_var, title = "", leg_name = "") {
  plot <- ggplot(data = data, aes_(x = ~long, y = ~lat, group = ~group, fill = as.name(fill_var))) +
    geom_polygon() +
    coord_quickmap() +
    labs(x = "",
         y = "",
         title = title) +
    #scale_fill_gradient(low = "orange", high = "purple") +
    scale_fill_distiller(name = leg_name, palette = "YlGnBu", labels = comma) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
    theme_bw()
  return(plot)
}

messages.subject: Best design-based way to maximize memory
messages.subject_clean: Best design-based way to maximize memory
messages.body_plain:
We can increase the amount of available memory for reading in files using something like:

options(shiny.maxRequestSize=30*1024^2)

which in this example hard codes to 30MB.

My shiny app is now shared across a large user group and as such I am trying to write the most generalizable, and "best" (in the design-sense), piece of code that varies the max limit depending on the amount of memory available on the user's machine.

So, what I am curious about is what is the best way to generalize the code above that accomplishes the following goals:

1) Increases the max memory to the maximum amount available to the user on their specific machine
2) Leaves in the appropriate amount of space for computational overhead

Thank you for your suggestions.

messages.subject: Best design-based way to maximize memory
messages.subject_clean: Best design-based way to maximize memory
messages.body_plain:
Hi Harold,

Memory usage can be wildly variable based on your packages in use and how many times you create copies of the data.

My experience is that for simpler applications you need about 4 to 6 times the original data frame size. However, 10 to 20 times is not unreasonable for more complex applications. Also, keep in mind that R plus Shiny Server and Node JS all have overhead (if on a server.)

With system commands, you could check your available memory headroom, divide by a factor, such as 6 and allow that as max upload size. Keep in mind that Windows can often allocate additional memory via automatic swapping to hard drive, depending on your PC setup.

I highly recommend reading Hadleys quick overview of memory usage in R: http://adv-r.had.co.nz/memory.html

Finally, I believe Microsoft has released a community version of the former Revolution Analytics "memory on disk" caching capabilities. I have not delved into this, so I may be off on this route. Check it at http://www.microsoft.com/en/server-cloud/products/r-server/

Best regards,
Stephen McDaniel

messages.subject: Strange Working Directory Behavior after Shiny Deploy
messages.subject_clean: Strange Working Directory Behavior after Shiny Deploy
messages.body_plain:
I just got done wrestling with some very strange shiny server behavior and I was wondering if anyone could explain it to me. Here's what happened:

I developed a shiny app locally. I had some data that was loaded from a data directory and some stuff in globals.R shared by the ui.R and server.R. I initially deployed my app to my local install of shiny server. Then I made some changes and decided that I should have deployed using svn rather than just copying over the files. I moved the existing folder containing my shiny app to a new folder called archive and then replaced the directory I had just created by checking out the new version from my svn repo. This is when I noticed things started to go wrong, but I had no idea what was causing it. Suddenly variables that I had created in my global.R file weren't being recognized on the server. The app worked perfectly fine on my local machine, then I would deploy via svn and it was like it wasn't reading my global.R properly. So I rewrote the app using renderUI instead of using globals and then I noticed it wasn't registering any changes to my data directory, which was populating the dashboard. It seemed like everything was out of sync. After a lot of debugging I finally printed the working directory of my server-side R session and I noticed that it was set to the archive folder I had made when cleared the way for the svn deploy. Then I tried moving this archive folder into my home directory and sure enough, the shiny app switched over to ~/archive. It was loading server.R and ui.R from the proper place /srv/shiny-server/appName, but the R working directory was following around the shiny app that was originally at that location. I can't wrap my head around how that would happen and was hoping someone smarter could break it down for me.

I realize that ran sort of long so here's a shorter list of steps:
Deployed app on shiny server by copying ui.R, server.R, global.R, and data_dir to /srv/shiny-server/appName
Renamed /srv/shiny-server/appName to /srv/shiny-server/archive
Redeployed app on shiny server using svn, to original location: /srv/shiny-server/appName
Noticed changes to global.R and contents of data_dir weren't being recognized. All changes to server.R and ui.R were recognized though
Printed out R working directory using shinyjs and noticed it was /srv/shiny-server/archive, the original deployment directory
Moved the original deploy again, and the working directory followed it
Restarted shiny server and problem went away

The whole time I was pointing to the same URL. Glad that I finally got it figured out, because it was driving me crazy all day. I did get to learn how to use renderUI so something good came out of it. If anyone can provide any insight that would be great.

messages.subject: Re: Strange Working Directory Behavior after Shiny Deploy
messages.subject_clean: Strange Working Directory Behavior after Shiny Deploy
messages.body_plain:
The problem basically is that Shiny sets its working directory (setwd) once on process startup, and you can think of it being "in" that directory from then on. If you move the directory, it doesn't matter to the R process that Shiny is running in--it moves with it. Only restarting the R process (which by default happens 5 seconds after the last user of that particular app disconnects), which you finally did when you restarted shiny-server, makes the app pick up the new directory at the original path.

I was having trouble imagining how to work around this, but you say that getwd() returns the new path after the directory is moved? This may be a helpful clue... we can try to call setwd if we notice an unexpected change in getwd.

On Fri, Jul 15, 2016 at 6:04 PM Mike Mehan <mme...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I just got done wrestling with some very strange shiny server behavior and I was wondering if anyone could explain it to me. Here's what happened:
>
>
> I developed a shiny app locally. I had some data that was loaded from a data directory and some stuff in globals.R shared by the ui.R and server.R. I initially deployed my app to my local install of shiny server. Then I made some changes and decided that I should have deployed using svn rather than just copying over the files. I moved the existing folder containing my shiny app to a new folder called archive and then replaced the directory I had just created by checking out the new version from my svn repo. This is when I noticed things started to go wrong, but I had no idea what was causing it. Suddenly variables that I had created in my global.R file weren't being recognized on the server. The app worked perfectly fine on my local machine, then I would deploy via svn and it was like it wasn't reading my global.R properly. So I rewrote the app using renderUI instead of using globals and then I noticed it wasn't registering any changes to my data directory, which was populating the dashboard. It seemed like everything was out of sync. After a lot of debugging I finally printed the working directory of my server-side R session and I noticed that it was set to the archive folder I had made when cleared the way for the svn deploy. Then I tried moving this archive folder into my home directory and sure enough, the shiny app switched over to ~/archive. It was loading server.R and ui.R from the proper place /srv/shiny-server/appName, but the R working directory was following around the shiny app that was originally at that location. I can't wrap my head around how that would happen and was hoping someone smarter could break it down for me.
>
> I realize that ran sort of long so here's a shorter list of steps:
> Deployed app on shiny server by copying ui.R, server.R, global.R, and data_dir to /srv/shiny-server/appName
> Renamed /srv/shiny-server/appName to /srv/shiny-server/archive
> Redeployed app on shiny server using svn, to original location: /srv/shiny-server/appName
> Noticed changes to global.R and contents of data_dir weren't being recognized. All changes to server.R and ui.R were recognized though
> Printed out R working directory using shinyjs and noticed it was /srv/shiny-server/archive, the original deployment directory
> Moved the original deploy again, and the working directory followed it
> Restarted shiny server and problem went away
>
> The whole time I was pointing to the same URL. Glad that I finally got it figured out, because it was driving me crazy all day. I did get to learn how to use renderUI so something good came out of it. If anyone can provide any insight that would be great.
>

messages.body_plain:
If I'm understanding this correctly, what you have seems pretty reasonable. I'd just put the callModule(slider_menu_item_shiny_X, ...) calls into an lapply, and put the lapply() inside a reactive(), and if necessary create another wrapper reactive() that extracts the slider values out of the list of reactive expressions, for convenience.

slider_reactives <- reactive({
  lapply(1:slider_length(), function(m) {
    callModule(slider_menu_item_shiny, sprintf("slider_menu_item_shiny_", m))
  })
})

slider_values <- reactive({
  lapply(slider_reactives(), function(r) r())
})

Note that this might cause problems if your slider_menu_item_shiny module (or a submodule called therein) sets up observers, as these would be duplicated over time as callModule gets invoked over and over again for these same IDs. Dealing with this would be a bit trickier and involve setting up and destroying only the modules that need to be added/removed from one value of slider_length() to another. But if you're only declaring outputs and reactives in these modules, it should be fine.

messages.subject: selectizeInput and reactive elements: how to avoid app updates while selecting items
messages.subject_clean: selectizeInput and reactive elements: how to avoid app updates while selecting items
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I developed a shiny app where I have code like:

# ui.R
# available_country is a list loaded before ui.R
selectizeInput("country", "Country", choices = available_countries, multiple = TRUE)

# server.R
data_to_plot <- reactive({
    active_data <- dplyr::filter(data, country %in% input$country)
    results <- complex_function(active_data)
    return(results)
})

The issue I am facing is that "data_to_plot" is updated every time I select something in the list of countries I build with selectize,
even though the selection might not be final. Is there a way to have shiny wait for the user to actually finish selecting items
before refreshing the value of data_to_plot?

Thanks a lot to all of you for the help!

Cheers,
Luca

messages.body_plain: No. Shiny has a reactivity model where an event is triggered for any change of the widget at all. It doesn't have particular events for when an input widget loses focus, unlike other programming languages for user interfaces. I hope that becomes possible to do in future versions.

messages.subject: Changing base layers in Leaflet for R without loosing the overlay
messages.subject_clean: Changing base layers in Leaflet for R without loosing the overlay
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to change the base layer in my Shiny App in a programatic way. Since I don't want to use the LayerControl of 'Leaflet' and rather want to have all the controls in one panel. I decided to use shinyjs and go with the toggleState for a button to switch forth and back between two base layers.

At the moment I am in the phase to figure out the principles of changing the base layer, and since there can be only one base layer visible it seem like I have to remove the tiles of the initially loaded base layer.

Doing so I can change the base layer at display, but at the same time the base layer is changed I am loosing the overlay. How can I avoid that?
When using the button again I can see in the flicker that the overlay is still there, but not on top of the base layer anymore.

You can find some sample code here <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/38454973/changing-base-layers-in-leaflet-for-r-without-loosing-the-overlay/38457949#38457949>, and some suggestions on how to deal with the problem, even though I don't understand how the suggestions are related to the problem.

Cheers Thomas

messages.subject: Re: observe & observeEvent
messages.subject_clean: observe & observeEvent
messages.body_plain:
If the code only has one reactive variable, then yes they're pretty similar with a few small differences (for example, observeEvent by default will ignore NULL values which can come in quite handy).  If you have multiple reactive values in the expression inside `observe()`, then you won't be able to easily achieve a similar behaviour with `observeEvent()` because you have to tell it what single reactive value to listen to

    data.frame(
      id = row(m)[idx],

  output$hist<-renderPlot({hist(df()$values)})

req(input$slider2)

output$allmaps <- renderPlot(

  },
  height = function() {

  }
)

Ohhhh. I just realized that you're using "vh" units, and the above only works with pixels.

OK. Using your original code you can probably do this:

       $('#allmaps').css('height', message).trigger('shown');

The trigger('shown') at the end is to cause Shiny to realize that something has happened that might have affected the layout of the page, so it will take the time to re-examine the visibility and size of all output elements and send any changed properties to the server.

messages.body_plain:
It's not clear to me what you're trying to do with your matrix. Do you want to sum the values in each row of the matrix, and display the result on the histogram?

As for the verbatimtextouput/slider - it works fine in the example below. Is this different from what you had?

ui <- fluidPage(

  sliderInput(inputId="adjust", label="Choose adjacency threshold", value=c(0.001, 0.9), min=0.0001, max=1),

  plotOutput("hist"),
  verbatimTextOutput("x")

)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  m<-cbind(c(0.05,0.01,3),c(2,3,4), c(4,5,6))

  df <- reactive({
    idx <- m > min(input$adjust) & m < max(input$adjust)

    data.frame(
      id = row(m)[idx],
      value = m[idx])
  })

  output$hist<-renderPlot({hist(df()$value)})

  output$x<-renderPrint({min(input$adjust)})

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

I'm trying to get the automatic file decompression of readr working in a shiny app, but I'm running into some issues. Here's a MWE for the app and two example files are:

mtcars.zip <https://www.dropbox.com/s/1uu1jyg7q5kgce8/mtcars.zip?dl=1>
library(shiny)
library(readr)

ui <- fluidPage(
   titlePanel("Test upload"),
   sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
        fileInput('file1', 'Upload csv file or zipped csv file')
      ),
      mainPanel(
         tableOutput("tabOut")
      )
   )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
   output$tabOut <- renderTable({
     inFile <- input$file1
     validate(
       need(!is.null(input$file1), "Please upload a data file")
     )
     dat <- read_csv(inFile$datapath)
     return(dat)
   })
}

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.body_plain:
I've found a solution that involves manually renaming the file.

Replace:

     dat <- read_csv(inFile$datapath)
     return(dat)

with:

input_file_format <- tools::file_ext(inFile$name)
new_file_name<-paste0(inFile$datapath,".",input_file_format)
file.rename(inFile$datapath, new_file_name)
dat = readr::read_csv(new_file_name)
return(dat)

Not sure if this is the best approach, but it's working for now.

Below is the code:

ui.R

dashboardPage(
    skin = "green",

    dashboardHeader(title = "UA LTV"),
    dashboardSidebar(
        sidebarMenu(
            id = "sidebarMenu",
            menuItem(
                text = "Prediction",

A similar question was asked here:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/TnG5KCnaG3U

And also here:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/20637248/shiny-4-small-textinput-boxes-side-by-side

You use div attributes to position. The following will give you what you're looking for:

library(shiny)
server <- function(input, output) {}

ui <- fluidPage(
  mainPanel(

    tags$div(class = "className", id = "idName",
      "Text Before",
      tags$input(id = "number", type="number", value = "5", min = "1", max="100"),
      "Text After"))

  )
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

More info:
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/html-tags.html

messages.subject: nested render* calls
messages.subject_clean: nested render* calls
messages.body_plain:
I've recently been building Shiny apps that alter their UI based on the user's input.
An example of how to do this was posted by W. Chang here: https://gist.github.com/wch/5436415/.
In that example, explicit outputs are created and named dynamically, via a call like `output[[plotname]] <- renderPlot(...)`.
Lazy evaluation then prevents any plots from being drawn than don't have the corresponding dynamic `plotOutput(plotname)` in the UI (populated via `renderUI`).

Below is an alternative that seems to be working for me and is much simpler in code, but perhaps more complicated when modeling out the reactive dependency chains:

##------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(shiny); library(DT)

buildTabPanel <- function(title) {
    tabPanel(title = title, DT::renderDataTable(iris))
}

ui <- fluidPage(sliderInput("n_tabs", label = "# Tabs", min = 1, max = 5, value = 2),
                uiOutput("outer"))

server <- function(input,output) {
    output$outer <- renderUI({
        tab_panels <- lapply(seq_len(input$n_tabs), function(i) buildTabPanel(i))
        do.call(tabsetPanel, tab_panels)
    })
}
##------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The `ui` holds the "outer" placeholder.
Then, the server's `renderUI` function dynamically builds each `tabPanel` (based on `input$n_tabs`) and populates it with a `renderDataTable`.
I was surprised this worked at all during my experimentation, but happily delighted that it did.
My only concern is that perhaps I've stumbled upon a design pattern that can cause problems with the reactive evaluation chain (since I'm not well-versed in the exact implementation details of the render* and other reactive functions).
Does anyone see any alarming flaws with this pattern?

Cheers,

-murat

messages.subject: Re: nested render* calls
messages.subject_clean: nested render* calls
messages.body_plain:
That's mostly fine. If you put a DT::renderDataTable() call (or most any other render call) directly in a server-generated UI, Shiny will implicitly insert a corresponding dataTableOutput() call for you in that location (with a randomly generated ID). This functionality was introduced to support Shiny R Markdown documents <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_shiny.html#inputs_and_outputs>. It does mean creating many outputs; while any outputs that aren't showing will be suspended (which you referred to as lazy evaluation), they can't be garbage collected because Shiny doesn't know for a fact that they're not coming back later. So you do have to watch out for memory leaks with this pattern.

messages.subject: Re: How to return a reactive expression from a module to the calling app?
messages.subject_clean: How to return a reactive expression from a module to the calling app?
messages.body_plain:
The ui1 function should not take `cond` as an input parameter. Instead, it should *return* the cond reactive expression as the return value, i.e. the last line of the function should simply be `cond` (or `return(cond)` if you want to be more explicit).

Then, `callModule(ui1, "ui1", cond)` should become: `cond <- callModule(ui1, "ui1")`

That should do it

messages.subject: Re: Scaling up Shiny apps
messages.subject_clean: Scaling up Shiny apps
messages.body_plain:
The core of R itself is single threaded, but there are libraries that allow for parallel execution across multiple cores/machines, and algorithms that can leverage multiple cores.  The answer to Xiachen's question is really dependent on what the code is trying to do.  If the code is single threaded, then a faster CPU on a physical server may make a difference, but my experience has been that the choice of libraries you use (for example there are many libraries that use Rcpp to call out C++ code) which are 100-1000x faster than their counterparts in R.

HTH

>

> > b) using C/C++/C#: has anyone tried to call C# from R on Linux?
> > c) faster CPU
> > d) lots of memory
> > e) physical server (I am running on a VM now)
> >
> > Any suggestion would be very helpful. Thanks very much!

messages.subject: Re: nested render* calls
messages.subject_clean: nested render* calls
messages.body_plain:
Ah, I see your point, thanks much for the insight. I now see why in the original Gist example uses the 'maximum number of outputs' design pattern.

Now purely wondering/conjecture for sake of discussion: would it conceptually be possible (i.e. easily within the existing Shiny code) to 'link' those auto-generated output IDs with a 'parent' output ID (or a random state-identifying token associated with the parent)?
Then, when the parent output is recomputed (and the token changes), all token-associated children are destroyed, gc()-ed, and then re-built dynamically (and linked to the new stateful token) as needed.
It'd be _almost_ as if the auto-generated output objects take a reactive dependency to the parent output object, with a special reactive destroying/gc()-ing behavior.

-m

On Thursday, July 28, 2016 at 12:10:40 AM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> That's mostly fine. If you put a DT::renderDataTable() call (or most any other render call) directly in a server-generated UI, Shiny will implicitly insert a corresponding dataTableOutput() call for you in that location (with a randomly generated ID). This functionality was introduced to support Shiny R Markdown documents <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_shiny.html#inputs_and_outputs>. It does mean creating many outputs; while any outputs that aren't showing will be suspended (which you referred to as lazy evaluation), they can't be garbage collected because Shiny doesn't know for a fact that they're not coming back later. So you do have to watch out for memory leaks with this pattern.
>
> On Wed, Jul 27, 2016 at 9:32 PM Murat Tasan <mmu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > I've recently been building Shiny apps that alter their UI based on the user's input.
> > An example of how to do this was posted by W. Chang here: https://gist.github.com/wch/5436415/.
> > In that example, explicit outputs are created and named dynamically, via a call like `output[[plotname]] <- renderPlot(...)`.
> > Lazy evaluation then prevents any plots from being drawn than don't have the corresponding dynamic `plotOutput(plotname)` in the UI (populated via `renderUI`).
> >
> > Below is an alternative that seems to be working for me and is much simpler in code, but perhaps more complicated when modeling out the reactive dependency chains:
> >
> > ##------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> > library(shiny); library(DT)
> >
> > buildTabPanel <- function(title) {
> >     tabPanel(title = title, DT::renderDataTable(iris))
> > }
> >
> > ui <- fluidPage(sliderInput("n_tabs", label = "# Tabs", min = 1, max = 5, value = 2),
> >                 uiOutput("outer"))
> >
> > server <- function(input,output) {
> >     output$outer <- renderUI({
> >         tab_panels <- lapply(seq_len(input$n_tabs), function(i) buildTabPanel(i))
> >         do.call(tabsetPanel, tab_panels)
> >     })
> > }
> > ##------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> >
> > The `ui` holds the "outer" placeholder.
> > Then, the server's `renderUI` function dynamically builds each `tabPanel` (based on `input$n_tabs`) and populates it with a `renderDataTable`.
> > I was surprised this worked at all during my experimentation, but happily delighted that it did.
> > My only concern is that perhaps I've stumbled upon a design pattern that can cause problems with the reactive evaluation chain (since I'm not well-versed in the exact implementation details of the render* and other reactive functions).
> > Does anyone see any alarming flaws with this pattern?
> >
> > Cheers,
> >
> > -murat

I have an interesting problem.  I am using ggtern package to draw the ternary diagrams.  I wrapped this in the Shiny library to enable users to select input parameters from the drop downs.  I could not get the current version of Shiny to draw the ggtern properly until I saw the following post:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/915

So I downgraded from the current version of shiny to the version 0.11.1 as recommended and the ternary diagram worked perfectly :)

The next step was for me to show the data frame in wrapped in a datatable using dataTableOutput and renderDataTable functions.  This sort of works but it even the official docs say that this is going to be dropped in the future and the recommendation is to use the new DT package.  So I installed the DT package but ran into problems.  The DT package requires shiny 0.12.0 or greater.

Is there anyway out of this situation?  As a Rails programmer, I am used to a bundler type solution where you can specify exact versions of gems to be used for a project.  I googled for a solution in R and could not find any.

Please advise.

Thanks.

Bharat

          "#FF7F00", "#FFFF33", "#A65628", "#F781BF", "#999999"))

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  # The selected file, if any

    # If no file is selected, don't do anything
    validate(need(input$file, message = FALSE))
    input$file

    read.csv(userFile()$datapath,

  # Combine the selected variables into a new data frame
  selectedData <- reactive({

messages.subject: selectizeInput difference in server-side and client-side mode reactions?
messages.subject_clean: selectizeInput difference in server-side and client-side mode reactions?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a rather complex logic for updating 4 interdependent selectizeInputs().

I spotted the huge difference in the behaviour after a Chrome update few weeks ago where selectize.js with large number of choices simply crashes.

So far so good, I knew about shiny's server-side option so I gave it a try and since that moment a cry :D

The whole dependency chain for my selectizeInputs broke and I have spent few days to isolate the problem.

Apparently, in client side mode after a field is updated with updateSelectizeInput()  the new value is immediately inserted in the UI and dependent observers are triggered once.
In server-side mode this happens in two steps where the selectizeInput is first cleared and then the new value is inserted.

The problem is that this way all dependencies of a certain field are triggered once with empty "" value and once after that with the correct value.
Between these 2 triggers all dependencies manage to mess up their own values a lot.

Please refer to the code and output below.

In serverMode = FALSE                                                 in Server Mode = TRUE

[1] "Item value is : " "apple"
[1] "is_item_in_choices..."
[1] "query_item_cat..."
[1] "does_item_exists..."
[1] "item_select_cat ..."
[1] "UPDATE_CAT_FROM_ITEM..."
[1] "UPDATE_CAT DONE!"
[1] "SELF UPDATE ITEM..."
[1] "ITEM after self update is: " "apple"
[1] "query_item_choices..."
[1] "CAT UPDATE ITEM..."                                         ###### as in client mode plus ######
                                                                                  [1] "Item value is : " ""
                                                                                  [1] "is_item_in_choices..."
                                                                                  [1] "Item value is : " "apple"
                                                                                  [1] "is_item_in_choices..."

Test procedure:
1. Start the app
2. choose category "B" or "C"
3. write "apple" in Item and click "Add.. apple"

Any suggestion or advise is highly appreciated :)

Cheers,
Aleks

serverMode = FALSE   # assign TRUE to see the difference

library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(

      # Application title
      titlePanel("Selectize Server-Side VS Cliend-Side Mode"),

      # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins
      sidebarLayout(
            sidebarPanel(
                  radioButtons(
                        inputId    = "cat"
                        , label    = "Category"
                        , choices  = list("A", "B", "C")
                        , selected = "A"
                        , inline   = TRUE
                        , width    = NULL
                  )
                  , selectizeInput(
                        inputId  = "item"
                        , label    = "Items"
                        , choices  = list()
                        , options  = list(
                              maxOptions     = 10
                              , placeholder  = 'Choose ...'
                              , preload      = TRUE
                              , create       = TRUE
                              , server       = serverMode
                        )
                  )
            ),

            # Show a plot of the generated distribution
            mainPanel(
                  plotOutput("distPlot")
            )
      )
))

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

      item_select_cat <- eventReactive(
            c(
                  does_item_exists()
            ),{
                  print("item_select_cat ...")
                  if(does_item_exists()) query_item_cat()
                  else NULL
            }, ignoreNULL = TRUE
      )

      observeEvent(
            item_select_cat()
            ,{
                  print("UPDATE_CAT_FROM_ITEM...")
                  updateRadioButtons(
                        session   = session
                        ,inputId  = 'cat'
                        ,selected = item_select_cat()
                  )
                  print("UPDATE_CAT DONE!")
            }
      )

      #########################################################
      ################# Self update chain #####################
      #########################################################

      is_item_in_choices <- eventReactive(
            c(
                  input$item
            )
            ,{
                  print(c("Item value is : ", input$item))
                  print("is_item_in_choices...")
                  if(input$item %in% query_item_choices() || input$item == "") NULL#FALSE # ||
                  else FALSE
            }
      )

      query_item_cat <- eventReactive(
            is_item_in_choices()
            ,{
                  print("query_item_cat...")
                  query$item_cat(input$item)
            }
      )

      does_item_exists <- eventReactive(
            query_item_cat()
            ,{
                  print("does_item_exists...")
                  if(is.null(query_item_cat())) FALSE
                  else TRUE
            }, ignoreNULL = FALSE
      )

      self_update_item <- observeEvent(
            {
                  does_item_exists()
            },{
                  print("SELF UPDATE ITEM...")
                  if(!does_item_exists()){
                        print("ITEM DOES NOT Exists!")
                        updateSelectizeInput(
                              session   = session
                              ,inputId  = 'item'
                              ,choices  = query_item_choices()
                              ,selected = 0
                              ,server   = serverMode
                        )
                  }
                  print(c("ITEM after self update is: ", input$item))
            }
      )

      #########################################################
      ################### UP update chain #####################
      #########################################################
      query_item_choices <- eventReactive(
            c(
                  input$cat
            ),{
                  print("query_item_choices...")
                  query$item(input$cat)
            }
      )

      cat_update_item <- observeEvent(
            {
                  query_item_choices()
            },{
                  print("CAT UPDATE ITEM...")

                  updateSelectizeInput(
                        session   = session
                        ,inputId  = 'item'
                        ,choices  = query_item_choices()
                        ,selected = input$item
                        ,server   = serverMode
                  )
            }
      )

})

query <-  list()

query$item_cat <- function(item = character()){
      switch (item
              , "apple"  = "A"
              , "pear"   = "A"
              , "banana" = "A"
              , "tomato" = "B"
              , "pepper" = "B"
              , "onion"  = "B"
              , "milk"   = "C"
              , "juice"  = "C"
              , "water"  = "C"
      )
}

query$item <- function(cat = character()){
      switch (cat
              ,"A" = c("apple", "pear", "banana")
              ,"B" = c("tomato", "pepper", "onion")
              ,"C" = c("milk", "juice", "water")
      )
}

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: How might I (recursively) rename multiple values in a data frame
messages.subject_clean: How might I (recursively) rename multiple values in a data frame
messages.body_plain:
I’m trying to rename multiple values in a data frame, using R, Shiny, and rhandsontable. A description of the problem follows.

Toy Data Frame:

100 observations of 3 variables. The variables are color, sampled from red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet;
ALeast, sampled from Orioles, RedSox, BlueJays, Yankees, and Rays; and
NewEngland, sampled from ME, VT, NH, MA, CT, and RI.

I’d like to be able to

rename every instance of ‘blue’ to read ‘cyan’, followed by
renaming every instance of ‘Yankees’ to read ‘Mets, followed by
renaming every instance of ‘ME’ to read ‘Maine’.

With the possibility of returning to any of the variables and continue with renaming.

In the real world example the number of variables and the values associated with each variable aren’t known ahead of time.

The current version of the Shiny app I’m building is attached. I’m using rhandsontable (https://github.com/jrowen/rhandsontable) to support the renaming, patterning the renaming steps after the rhandsontable_datafile (rhandsontable/inst/examples) example provided by jrowen.

I am able to select one of the three variables and rename its values. I am not able to then select one of the other two variables and proceed with renaming values. Once I select the ‘Commit’ button the rhandsontable no longer updates to reflect the selected variable.

Any help / suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

.....code.....

##

## Home > R > brickyard > FindAndReplace

##

## table renaming based on the work of Jonathan Owen

## [github] jrowen / rhandsontable & examples therein

library(shiny)

library(magrittr)

library(rhandsontable)

library(dplyr)

##### build toy data frame

colors <- data.frame(sample(c('red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'green', 'blue', 'indigo', 'violet'),

                            100, replace = TRUE))

colnames(colors) <- c("color")

colors$color <- as.character(colors$color)

teams <- data.frame(sample(c("Orioles", "RedSox", "BlueJays", "Yankees", "Rays"),

                           100, replace = TRUE))

colnames(teams) <- c("ALeast")

teams$ALeast <- as.character(teams$ALeast)

states <- data.frame(sample(c("ME", "VT", "NH", "MA", "CT", "RI"),

                            100, replace = TRUE))

colnames(states) <- c("NewEngland")

states$NewEngland <- as.character(states$NewEngland)

df <- data.frame(cbind(colors, teams, states))

vars <- names(df)

##

## UI

##

ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(

  uiOutput("choose_var"),

  DT::dataTableOutput(outputId = "recoding"),

  actionButton("commitButton", "Commit"),

  rHandsontableOutput("hot"),

  DT::dataTableOutput(outputId = "newVars")

  ))

##

## SERVER

##

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {

##### choose variable for value renaming

  output$choose_var <- renderUI({

    radioButtons(inputId = "var",

                 label = "Select column to recode",

                 choices = vars)

    })

  output$selectedVar <- renderText(input$var)

##### build a (reactive) 2-column data frame with a variable's unique values

##### the idea being the left hand column presents the initial values, and the

##### right hand column presents values the user is meant rename ... initially,

##### both columns hold the same content

#####

##### these renamed values will be used in updating the entire data frame

#####

  recodeValues <- reactive({

    if(is.null(input$var)) {return()}

    uniqueVars <- df %>% select_(input$var) %>% unique()

    convert <- cbind(uniqueVars, uniqueVars)

    colnames(convert) <- c("original", "convert")

    convert

    })

##### display the data frame - making sure data is updating

  output$recoding <- DT::renderDataTable({

    recodeValues()

    })

##### the following code is based on Jonathan Owen's rhandsontable package

##### see his rhandsontable_datafile example

  fname = tempfile()

  values = list()

  setHot = function(x) values[["hot"]] <<- x

  observe({

    input$commitButton

    if (!is.null(values[["hot"]])) {

      write.csv(values[["hot"]], fname)

      print(fname)

##### use the recoded values to rename values throughout the entire data frame

      recodes <- read.csv(fname, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

      for(i in 1:nrow(recodes)){

        if(recodes[i,2] != recodes[i,3]){

          df[df == recodes[i,2]] <- recodes[i,3]

        }

      }

      output$newVars <- DT::renderDataTable({

        df

      })

      }

    })

  output$hot = renderRHandsontable({

    if (!is.null(input$hot)) {

      DF = hot_to_r(input$hot)

    } else {

        if(is.null(input$var)) {return()}

      DF = recodeValues()

      }

    setHot(DF)

    rhandsontable(DF) %>%

      hot_table(highlightCol = TRUE, highlightRow = TRUE)

  })

  }

  )

##

## Run the application

##

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
